name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Democratic-leaning district (D+6) with a long-serving incumbent
Keating holds a large fundraising edge in cash on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings are available
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's Democratic lean, Keating's incumbency and roughly tenfold cash advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent for the Democrat. With no polls or ratings suggesting competition, the fundamentals-based margin of about 19 points stands.
model.watch: A wave of outside spending against Keating or a sharply nationalized environment could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would require an unprecedented shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts's 9th District leans Democratic, and Bill Keating has held the seat since 2011. He enters the general election with a clear financial edge, having raised about $535,000 and holding roughly $512,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised about $213,000 with $52,000 available. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, but prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent.

The combination of a favorable district, an entrenched incumbent, and a wide fundraising gap leaves little evidence of a competitive race. MacAllister would need a dramatic shift in the political environment or a surge of outside spending to close a deficit of this size. As it stands, the available signals point to Keating returning for another term.
